snapshot.title: TNPSC Unit 9: Education & Health in TN
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Unit 9 Hook: Kamaraj: Mid-day. MGR: Nutritious. GER: 51%. Health: Top. Illam Thedi Kalvi: Doorstep. Samacheer: Uniform.

quick_notes.title: Education Milestones
quick_notes.detail: K. Kamaraj (Kingmaker) introduced Mid-day meals (1956). MGR introduced Nutritious Meal Scheme (1982). High GER (Higher Ed) ~51.4%.
quick_notes.explanation: K. Kamaraj, who was known as the Kingmaker, started the Mid-day Meals program in 1956, which gave free lunches to school children to encourage them to attend school. Later, in 1982, MGR, whose full name is M. G. Ramachandran, introduced the Nutritious Meal Scheme, which provided a more balanced and healthy meal to students. GER stands for Gross Enrollment Ratio, which is the percentage of people in a certain age group who are enrolled in a particular level of education. For higher education, which means college and university studies, the GER in Tamil Nadu is about 51.4 percent, meaning that roughly half of the people in the typical college-age group are actually studying in higher education institutions.

quick_notes.title: Health Infrastructure
quick_notes.detail: 3-tier system: PHC, District Hospitals, Medical Colleges. 1st State to enact "Right to Health".
quick_notes.explanation: Health Infrastructure refers to the system of medical facilities in India. The system has three main levels. The first level is the Primary Health Centre, or PHC, which is a small clinic in rural areas that provides basic medical care. The second level is District Hospitals, which are larger hospitals that serve a whole district and offer more advanced treatments. The third level is Medical Colleges, which are large teaching hospitals that train doctors and provide the most specialized care. The first state in India to officially pass a law giving citizens the right to health services, called the Right to Health, was Rajasthan.

quick_notes.title: Health Indicators
quick_notes.detail: Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) and Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) are significantly lower than the national average.
quick_notes.explanation: Health Indicators are measures used to assess the health of a population. Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is the number of deaths of babies under one year old for every 1000 live births. Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) is the number of women who die due to pregnancy or childbirth for every 100,000 live births. In Tamil Nadu, both the IMR and the MMR are much lower than the national average of India. This means that fewer infants and mothers die in Tamil Nadu compared to the country as a whole, showing that the state has better healthcare facilities and services.

quick_notes.title: Samacheer Kalvi
quick_notes.detail: Uniform system of school education introduced to bridge the gap between different streams.
quick_notes.explanation: Samacheer Kalvi is a Tamil phrase that means Uniform Education System. It is a single, common school education system introduced by the Tamil Nadu government to bring all students under one curriculum, removing the differences between various school boards like Matriculation, Anglo-Indian, CBSE, and the old State Board. Before this system, students from different streams studied different subjects, which created a gap in learning levels and made transfers between schools difficult. The Samacheer Kalvi system makes sure every student in Tamil Nadu, from Class 1 to Class 12, studies the same syllabus in core subjects like Tamil, English, Mathematics, Science, and Social Science. This single stream of education ensures all students have equal learning opportunities, and it allows a child to move from one school to another without losing their place in the syllabus.

quick_notes.title: Important Schemes
quick_notes.detail: Moovalur Ramamirtham (Higher ed for girls), Illam Thedi Kalvi (Post-pandemic education).
quick_notes.explanation: The Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme provides financial assistance to girls from poor families so they can continue their education after school, covering tuition fees and other expenses for college or university. The Illam Thedi Kalvi scheme, which means Education at the Doorstep, was launched after the COVID-19 pandemic to help school students who fell behind in their studies by sending trained volunteers to their homes for free tutoring. Both schemes are run by the Tamil Nadu government to support students who might otherwise drop out of school or be unable to afford higher education.
